title: Sell Mineral Rights in Fruita, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights Near Fruita, CO | Grand Valley Piceance
metaDescription: Own minerals near Fruita in Mesa County's Grand Valley? We evaluate Piceance Basin interests and make a direct, no-obligation offer.
heroLead: Fruita and the surrounding Grand Valley are known first for peach and fruit orchards, but the mineral estate underneath much of this Mesa County farmland has been part of the Piceance Basin story for decades.
intro: Agriculture, not oil and gas, has always been the dominant land use around Fruita, which means mineral ownership here is often lightly documented: a family kept the minerals when selling or leasing farmland, and nobody has revisited the paperwork since. That is common and easy for us to work through.

Piceance gas activity around Grand Junction and the broader Grand Valley has run in cycles tied to natural gas prices, with more concentrated development historically closer to Parachute and Rifle to the east than directly around Fruita itself.

sections.heading: Farm-first land, mineral estate underneath
paragraphs: A lot of Fruita-area deeds only mention the mineral estate in passing, buried in older farm transfer language. We read the actual conveyance language carefully to confirm whether a severance happened and what it covers before quoting anything.

sections.heading: Distance from the core matters
paragraphs: Because the more concentrated Piceance drilling has historically clustered farther east, Fruita-area acreage tends to be lighter on production history. We price accordingly, weighing comparable regional lease activity more heavily than decline-curve math when there is no well on the specific tract.

sections.heading: If your family has old lease paperwork
paragraphs: Even an expired or dormant lease tells us something useful about historical operator interest in the acreage. Send us whatever paperwork you have, even if it looks outdated, and we will factor it into the valuation.

sections.heading: What if the mineral estate was never actually severed
paragraphs: Not every Fruita-area farm deed severed the minerals. Sometimes a family sold the entire estate, surface and minerals together, and there is nothing separate left to sell. We check this first, since it is better to know early than to assume you own something you do not.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling right around Fruita?
faqs.answer: Less than farther east toward Parachute and Rifle. We check your specific tract's history rather than assuming based on the general area.

faqs.question: My deed barely mentions mineral rights. What do I do?
faqs.answer: Send it to us anyway. We read older conveyance language carefully to confirm what was actually severed.

faqs.question: Does an old, expired lease still matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, it shows past operator interest, which we weigh even if the lease itself has lapsed.

faqs.question: How do I know if my family actually kept the mineral rights?
faqs.answer: We read your deed's exact language, since severance has to be explicitly reserved. If it was not, the mineral estate transferred along with the surface.
